title: GitHub - physicsrob/torchwright: A compiler that transforms computation graphs into the weights of a transformer
excerpt: A compiler that transforms computation graphs into the weights of a transformer - physicsrob/torchwright
content_html:
torchwright is a compiler that transforms computation graphs into the weights of a transformer. You define a computation graph in ordinary Python, and torchwright produces the weights of a transformer that executes it. There is no training anywhere in the pipeline. Compiled models are packaged, by default, as ordinary transformers checkpoints in the Phi-3 architecture: AutoModelForCausalLM loads them with no custom code and no trust_remote_code.

This README covers the tool; the intro post covers how it came to exist and how the constructions were derived, from the ReLU primitives to a stock Phi-3 checkpoint.

Example

The graph in examples/binary_increment.py parses a binary string and increments it, carry propagation included. Compiling it produces an ordinary Hugging Face checkpoint:

from examples.binary_increment import create_network_parts, D_MODEL, D_HEAD
from torchwright import compile_hf_bundle

output_node, embedding = create_network_parts()
compile_hf_bundle(output_node, embedding, "binary_increment_hf_bundle",
                  d=D_MODEL, d_head=D_HEAD, optimize=1)

The result is a directory with safetensors, config, and tokenizer which loads like any transformers checkpoint:

from transformers import pipeline

generate = pipeline("text-generation", model="binary_increment_hf_bundle")
print(generate("1011\n", return_full_text=False)[0]["generated_text"])
# 1100

The compiler schedules this graph into a 16-layer decoder at hidden size 512 (the d=D_MODEL argument). Every weight is computed from the source graph. Nothing was trained. Compiling this example takes under ten seconds on a laptop CPU.

How it works

A torchwright program is a computation graph: ordinary Python wiring op calls into a DAG of nodes, with token embeddings at the leaves and one output node at the root.

Ops come in three groups: linear ops (add, subtract, concat, etc), attention ops (latch a value at a marker position, read a fixed offset back, argmax/argmin/mean over positions), and nonlinear ops (compare, select, multiply, etc).

The nonlinear ops are built from the transformer's FFN activation function, so choosing an activation means choosing an op library. torchwright.ops.relu constructs every nonlinear op from ReLU sublayers; torchwright.ops.swiglu constructs the same ops from gated SwiGLU sublayers, and is what the Phi-3 output uses. A graph imports from exactly one, and the compiler rejects a graph that mixes them.

The compiled computation lives in the residual stream. Every value the graph computes owns a set of columns there for as long as anything downstream still needs it; columns need not be contiguous, and concatenation is logical rather than physical. A sublayer can only add to the stream, and that one fact drives the compilation scheme: a new value lands in zeroed columns (0 + new = new), a value nothing needs anymore is cancelled by writing its negation (v + (−v) = 0), which frees its columns for reuse, and the graph's additions are implemented on the skip connection itself, costing no extra columns.

Every op compiles down to concrete weights living in attention heads or rows of FFN sublayers. A scheduler assigns every node to a layer:

  • optimize=0, the default, places nodes with a heuristic
  • optimize=1–3 uses a constraint-programming solver (CP-SAT, from Google OR-Tools) that minimizes layer count

Prior work

The idea of hand-built transformer weights is not new. RASP defines a language whose primitives map onto transformer sublayers, and Tracr compiles RASP programs into actual weights. torchwright differs at both ends: programs are arbitrary computation graphs written in ordinary Python instead of RASP, and the output targets a stock Phi-3 architecture, rather than a custom transformer model (with no norm).

Install

Python 3.10 or later.

pip install "torchwright[hf]"

Or from source:

git clone https://github.com/physicsrob/torchwright
cd torchwright
uv sync --extra hf

Core dependencies are torch, onnx, ortools, and pydantic. The hf extra adds transformers and safetensors for the Hugging Face output path. Running the ONNX output additionally needs an onnxruntime: install the onnxruntime package for CPU, or the gpu extra for onnxruntime-gpu.

Verification

Some of the constructions are exact, but plenty are piecewise-linear approximations. Correctness gets measured rather than assumed. Every approximated operation is checked against its exact-math reference, and the resulting error bounds are committed to the repository (docs/op_noise_data.json); the test suite fails if the committed numbers drift from what the code measures. Graph nodes can carry assert predicates. During development each assert is checked against the exact reference evaluation and again during debug forward passes of the compiled model. One that passes in exact math but fires when compiled points at exactly the operation where approximation error exceeded its budget. Finally, torchwright.debug.probe.probe_compiled diffs a compiled transformer node-by-node against direct evaluation of the source graph.

Per-op bounds are measured on each op's intended input ranges and do not compose through chains of ops; chain-level questions go to probe_compiled.

Examples

Twelve example graphs live in examples/:

  • adder_1digit parses "A+B\n", single-digit addition; the smallest complete program.
  • adder 3-digit addition: each digit pair goes through a lookup table and carries propagate right-to-left, pencil-and-paper style.
  • adder_v2 the same adder a different way: digits become numbers, one add, numbers become digits.
  • binary_increment the example above.
  • caesar_cipher shift cipher; the shift amount is a runtime input digit.
  • sort_digits_v1 sorts a digit string ascending, one digit per autoregressive step.
  • range_printer a two-level loop: iterate items, and for each item iterate a range of values.
  • fibonacci autoregressive: each number is computed from the model's own previously emitted tokens.
  • calculator_simple +, -, * on multi-digit integers, one lookup table and one fold at a time.
  • calculator_advanced the same functions at logarithmic depth, the way a hardware multiplier does it.
  • calculator_memorize computes nothing: every answer is a memorized fact.
  • calculator_scratchpad streams the serial carry/borrow work out as visible tokens and reads it back, so compiled depth stays flat as operand length grows.

Examples that define create_network_parts() compile to a bundle with uv run python -m examples.compile <name>.

Limitations

  • Only fp32 is supported.
  • With RMSNorm on (the default), supported hidden sizes (d) are any multiple of 1024 up to 16384, or any power of two; other widths raise. See docs/rms_norm_dmodel.md.
  • The KV cache is static: sequence length is fixed at export (max_seq_len, default 512), and overrunning it raises.

Further reading

  • Introducing torchwright -- the story and the constructions, from ReLU derivations to stock Phi-3.
  • docs/optimization_guide.md -- reducing layer count and parameter cost when compiling a graph.
  • docs/cpsat_scheduler.md -- the constraint-programming scheduler: model, objective, warm starts.
  • docs/affine_bounds.md -- how value bounds propagate through the graph.
  • docs/numerical_noise.md -- measured per-op approximation error (generated from docs/op_noise_data.json).

Development

make lint (ruff + mypy) and make test-local FILE=tests/... (single-file pytest) run anywhere.

Currently the full suite, make test, is designed to run on Modal, sharded across GPU containers (and thus needs a Modal account).

make measure-noise regenerates the committed per-op noise data.

CI runs on every push and pull request: make lint, plus a smoke test that compiles an example on CPU and checks its generated output.

License

Apache-2.0.

content_html_zh:
torchwright 是一个将计算图转换为变压器权重的编译器。 您可以在普通 Python 中定义一个计算图，然后 torchwright 会生成执行它的转换器的权重。 管道中没有任何培训。 默认情况下，编译的模型被打包为 Phi-3 架构中的普通 Transformer 检查点：AutoModelForCausalLM 加载它们时不使用自定义代码，也不使用 trust_remote_code。

本自述文件涵盖了该工具；这篇介绍文章介绍了它是如何存在的以及如何派生结构，从 ReLU 原语到库存 Phi-3 检查点。

例子

example/binary_increment.py 中的图解析二进制字符串并递增它，包括进位传播。 编译它会产生一个普通的 Hugging Face 检查点：

from examples.binary_increment import create_network_parts, D_MODEL, D_HEAD
from torchwright import compile_hf_bundle

output_node, embedding = create_network_parts()
compile_hf_bundle(output_node, embedding, "binary_increment_hf_bundle",
                  d=D_MODEL, d_head=D_HEAD, optimize=1)

结果是一个包含安全张量、配置和分词器的目录，它像任何变压器检查点一样加载：

from transformers import pipeline

generate = pipeline("text-generation", model="binary_increment_hf_bundle")
print(generate("1011\n", return_full_text=False)[0]["generated_text"])
# 1100

编译器将此图调度到隐藏大小 512（d=D_MODEL 参数）的 16 层解码器中。 每个权重都是根据源图计算的。 没有任何训练。 在笔记本电脑 CPU 上编译此示例只需不到十秒。

它是如何运作的

torchwright 程序是一个计算图：普通的 Python 将操作调用连接到节点的 DAG 中，在叶子处有令牌嵌入，在根处有一个输出节点。

操作分为三组：线性操作（加、减、连接等）、注意操作（在标记位置锁存值、读取固定偏移量、位置上的 argmax/argmin/mean）和非线性操作（比较、选择、乘法等）。

非线性运算是根据 Transformer 的 FFN 激活函数构建的，因此选择激活就意味着选择运算库。 torchwright.ops.relu 从 ReLU 子层构造每个非线性操作； torchwright.ops.swiglu 从门控 SwiGLU 子层构造相同的操作，并且是 Phi-3 输出使用的操作。 一张图恰好从一个图导入，编译器会拒绝混合它们的图。

编译后的计算存在于残余流中。 只要下游仍然需要它，图表计算的每个值都拥有一组列；列不必是连续的，并且串联是逻辑上的而不是物理上的。 子层只能添加到流中，这一事实驱动了编译方案：一个新值落在归零的列中 (0 + new = new)，通过写入其否定 (v + (−v) = 0) 来取消不再需要的值，从而释放其列以供重用，并且图的添加是在跳过连接本身上实现的，无需额外的列。

每个操作都会编译为存在于注意力头或 FFN 子层行中的具体权重。 调度程序将每个节点分配给一个层：

  • optimize=0，默认值，使用启发式方法放置节点
  • optimize=1–3 使用约束规划求解器（CP-SAT，来自 Google OR-Tools）来最小化层数

之前的工作

手工制作变压器配重的想法并不新鲜。 RASP 定义了一种语言，其原语映射到转换器子层，Tracr 将 RASP 程序编译为实际权重。 torchwright 在两端都有所不同：程序是用普通 Python 而不是 RASP 编写的任意计算图，并且输出目标是库存 Phi-3 架构，而不是自定义变压器模型（没有规范）。

安装

Python 3.10 或更高版本。

pip install "torchwright[hf]"

或者从来源：

git clone https://github.com/physicsrob/torchwright
cd torchwright
uv sync --extra hf

核心依赖项是 torch、onnx、ortools 和 pydantic。 hf extra 为 Hugging Face 输出路径添加了变压器和安全张量。 运行 ONNX 输出还需要 onnxruntime：为 CPU 安装 onnxruntime 软件包，或为 onnxruntime-gpu 安装 gpu extra。

确认

有些结构是精确的，但很多是分段线性近似。 正确性是通过测量而不是假设来实现的。 每个近似运算都会根据其精确数学参考进行检查，并将生成的误差范围提交到存储库 (docs/op_noise_data.json)；如果提交的数字偏离代码测量的数字，则测试套件将失败。 图节点可以携带断言谓词。 在开发过程中，每个断言都会根据准确的参考评估进行检查，并在编译模型的调试前向传递过程中再次进行检查。 一个传递精确数学但在编译时触发的函数恰好指向近似误差超出其预算的操作。 最后，torchwright.debug.probe.probe_compiled 将已编译的变压器与源图的直接评估逐个节点进行比较。

每个操作的边界是在每个操作的预期输入范围上测量的，并且不通过操作链组成；链级问题转到probe_compiled。

示例

十二个示例图位于示例/中：

  • adder_1digit 解析“A+B\n”，个位数加法；最小的完整程序。
  • 加法器 3 位加法：每个数字对都经过查找表并以铅笔和纸的方式从右到左传播。
  • adder_v2 同样是加法器，方式不同：数字变成数字，一加，数字变成数字。
  • 上面的例子是binary_increment。
  • caesar_cipher 移位密码；移位量是运行时输入数字。
  • sort_digits_v1 按升序对数字字符串进行排序，每个自回归步骤一位数字。
  • range_printer 一个两级循环：迭代项目，并为每个项目迭代一个值范围。
  • 斐波那契自回归：每个数字都是根据模型自己先前发出的标记计算的。
  • Calculator_simple 对多位整数进行+、-、*，一次查找一个表并折叠一次。
  • Calculator_advanced 在对数深度上实现相同的功能，就像硬件乘法器的方式一样。
  • Calculator_memorize 不计算任何内容：每个答案都是一个记住的事实。
  • 计算器_scratchpad将串行进位/借位计算结果作为可见标记进行流式传输并将其读回，因此随着操作数长度的增长，编译深度保持平坦。

定义 create_network_parts() 的示例使用 uv run python -m Examples.compile <name> 编译为捆绑包。

局限性

  • 仅支持 fp32。
  • 当 RMSNorm 打开（默认）时，支持的隐藏大小 (d) 是 1024 到 16384 的任意倍数，或 2 的任意幂；其他宽度升高。 请参阅 docs/rms_norm_dmodel.md。
  • KV 缓存是静态的：序列长度在导出时固定（max_seq_len，默认 512），并且会引发溢出。

进一步阅读

  • 介绍 torchwright——故事和构造，从 ReLU 推导到库存 Phi-3。
  • docs/optimization_guide.md -- 编译图时减少层数和参数成本。
  • docs/cpsat_scheduler.md -- 约束编程调度程序：模型、目标、热启动。
  • docs/affine_bounds.md -- 值边界如何在图表中传播。
  • docs/numerical_noise.md -- 测量的每个操作近似误差（从 docs/op_noise_data.json 生成）。

发展

制作 lint (ruff + mypy) 并制作 test-local FILE=tests/... （单文件 pytest）在任何地方运行。

目前，完整的套件 make test 被设计为在 Modal 上运行，跨 GPU 容器分片（因此需要一个 Modal 帐户）。

makemeasure-noise 重新生成提交的每操作噪声数据。

CI 在每个推送和拉取请求上运行：make lint，加上烟雾测试，在 CPU 上编译示例并检查其生成的输出。
